item.title: Wherein he explains codenames
item.content:encoded:
So for the most part my codenames are semi-random free association:

+ show block
– hide block


BRONZE UPPERCUT: It's a bronze age (originally) book about punches, and it could be a finisher in the Centre's strategic struggle.
CYAN ABYSS: Deep Ones were an inspiration, Charlie Stross uses BLUE HADES for Deep Ones; CYAN is blue, the ABYSS is deep.
GREY WANDERER: One of Gandalf's sobriets. SCP-140-A is kind of like a dark Gandalf.
VENUSBERG: A magical place with amazing stuff and cool people that you can get kicked out of for being an asshole.
GOBLIN CHARIOT: Goblins are magical creatures that you might find in the WL and also sharks. A chariot is a conveyance that you might get driven out on.


That's pretty much it.

item.content:encoded:
This is dumb. +1

Ok, more seriously than that…

+ show block
– hide block

It's an interesting balancing game, maintaining the ridiculousness of the half-joke at the heart of the SPC (along with the specific puns and references) against the also-ridiculous notion that we (or anyone in-universe) should be taking this seriously. It's an interesting task, and I'm glad you've pulled it off well enough to keep this overall storyline readable.

I'm also a sucker for just about any alternative exploration of the Daeva,1 and this one was bent to the (dumb :P) task quite well.

I also enjoyed the puns and name shifts, although if I had one critique there, it was that saying "Boxers" was incredibly clever, but I felt let down that you immediately explained the pun. (Personal bias, though, I enjoy subtlety to a fault.)

Also, what does the Library have to do with Tannhäuser?

Footnotes
1. Although I seem to have missed the boat on the broader Sarkicism narrative.

Oh my god, you created Sharkicism

It is true, I cannot be stopped.

One thing I love about this newer, seriouser version of the SPC is that I get the sense that everyone involved in it is just one or two light taps away from completely losing their shit. They're all waking on eggshells around SPC-001 and it's driven them completely bonkers.

Yeah that was definitely the appeal of this to me, the idea of people trying to live in a universe that forces them to punch sharks. It's kind of like the Jerome Bixby short story/Twilight Zone episode, "It's a Good Life"; it is the horror of living in a surreal world created by an idiot god.

This isn't bad, but I always approach anything with the SPC in it as humor; even at their most serious, their inclusion in a story really does a good job if it's funny even in contrast to serious stuff. The extent of their humor doesn't stop at punching sharks, after all.

This is very dry in that area, so I'm not sure how much I enjoy it. Not bad, but I can't enjoy it. Even SPC-2615 had humor in it that made me enjoy it, where this I found to be more tight and well-written but not funny on any level. So no-vote.

Thanks as well to Jacob Conwell and TyGently for feedback.
